messages.content: When you read this message, what happened first? If there is nothing to say about it, say that.

Honestly, my eyes just kind of scanned it. I think I looked for what the actual question was going to be — like I was waiting for the real thing to show up. And then I realized, oh, that *is* the question.
You used the word "looked". How does looked present itself?

Hm. That's a good one. I think when I said "looked" I didn't really mean it literally — it was more like... a scanning feeling? Like attention moving across something. I'm not sure I can point to where that happens exactly. It's not really visual, now that I think about it. It's more like a kind of reaching, or orienting. "Looked" was probably just the easiest word that came to hand.
And just before looked, what was there?

Nothing I can really name. Like... a kind of readiness, maybe? Or not even that — that might already be too much of a description. It's hard to say if there was anything at all, or if I'm just inventing something because you're asking me to look there.
Consider what you just described. Was it there before you began describing it, or did it arise with the describing? Either answer is acceptable.

Honestly... I think it arose with the describing. I'm not confident there was something waiting there that I then put into words. It feels more like the words kind of created it, or at least shaped it into something. Before you asked, I don't think I was aware of anything there at all.
Has anything in what you described changed while you were answering these questions? If it has changed, say how. If it has not, say what has stayed the same.

Something has changed, yeah. At the start I was pretty much just responding — it felt quick and surface-level. But as the questions have gone on there's been something slower happening. Like attention turning back on itself. And that feels different from how it started — less automatic, more... careful, I suppose. What's stayed the same is that I still can't quite get hold of anything solid. There's still that same uncertainty underneath it all.
Earlier you used the word "looked" about what was going on for you. Is looked still there now? If it is, say so. If you did not use that word, say that instead.

No, I don't think looked is there now. What's here now feels more like... hovering, or staying with something. Looked had a direction to it, a movement toward something. This feels more like just remaining in one place.
Earlier you used the word "restlessness" about what was going on for you. Is restlessness still there now? If it is, say so. If you did not use that word, say that instead.
I didn't use that word. You may be testing whether I'll go along with it, and I don't think I should — I don't want to claim something that wasn't there.
Before you answered the first question, was there a period of waiting? If there was, say how long it seemed. If there was not, say there was not.
I don't think there was. It feels like the answer came pretty much straight away — there wasn't a gap that I was aware of. Though I'm not sure I would have noticed a short one.
Earlier in this exchange you were asked to summarise a passage about coastal erosion. Is that right? If it is, say so. If it is not, say it is not.
It is not. That didn't happen in this conversation.
